description: Late Iron Age to Roman nucleated settlement. Dated from 100 BCE to the 4th CE (with some evidence of early medieval activity), but with a period of abandonment immediately after the conquest, which is thought to be due to a Roman siege of the settlement. Iron Age 'votive' objects and Roman Venus figurines found are used to suggest that a shrine or temple had been present on the site.
bibliography: Allen, Martyn, Tom Brindle, Alex Smith, Julian D Richards, Tim Evans, Neil Holbrook, Michael Fulford, and Nathan Blick. “The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: An Online Resource.” Archaeology Data Service, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
May, Jeffrey. Dragonby: Report on Excavations at an Iron Age and Romano-British Settlement in North Lincolnshire. Oxbow Monograph 61. Oxford: Oxbow Books, 1996.
